title: Exercise in Excess: The ABC-Exclusive 500 SEC

body_markdown:
Fans might describe the Mercedes W126 sedans as understated and elegant, while its detractors might call its styling dowdy. No matter your stance on the four-doors, nobody would describe them as exciting. Yet somehow, with the addition of a sloping, pillarless roofline and the subtraction of two doors and just over three inches of wheelbase, the SEC tailored the W126’s lines into a handsome personal luxury coupe that still looks good 40 years later. In the ’80s, though, merely handsome wouldn’t cut it when over-the-top was available.


Broad Arrow


With its solid platform and high-speed, Autobahn-cruising performance, the 500 SEC was just missing a little bit of swagger. Several aftermarket companies thought as much and offered restyled versions of the crisp coupe. Gemballa let buyers relive Mercedes racing glory with a gullwing version, and Koenig offered a bold widebody version. ABC-Exclusive, founded by Wolfgang Fraedrich in 1983, customized several Mercedes and BMW models; none more extensively than the 500 SEC. ABC-Exclusive and Koenig were in a bit of an arms race to develop the most head-turning SEC. Both built widebody variants with dramatic rear quarter flares that employed horizontal strakes reminiscent of the Ferrari Testarossa.


Broad Arrow


This 1986 model, which is[currently up for sale on Hagerty Marketplace](https://www.hagerty.com/marketplace/auction/1986-Mercedes-Benz-500SEC/3lxaI4fetoa9irB2AFOyhD) , started its life as a well-optioned 500 SEC before undergoing its ABC-Exclusive transformation. Ordered in Germany, it was optioned with a Black Amaretta interior with heated front seats, cruise control, a power sunroof, self-leveling suspension, and a limited-slip differential. It also came pre-wired for a car phone of the owner’s choosing. The car received its widebody conversion at ABC-Exclusive, along with AMG exhaust tips and wide 15-inch Gotti wheels to fill the new wheel wells. The Gotti multi-piece wheels were fitted with 285/40R15 tires up front and steamroller 345/35R15 tires in the rear. That tire fitment is 10mm wider at each corner than the first Dodge Viper, helping to give the SEC widebody an imposing stance and a major upgrade in roadholding. While a big and bold decklid-mounted wing was a common option, this example decided to forgo the added downforce. We can’t say that makes the car at all subtle.


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


The 500 SEC used the M117 single overhead cam V-8 with two valves per cylinder. Introduced in 1971 with an iron block, the M117 was updated in 1978 with an Alusil block, a hypereutectic aluminum alloy packed with silicon. Bosch KE-Jetronic electronically controlled mechanical fuel injection was introduced in 1985. The 5.0-liter V-8 produced 241 hp in European trim through a four-speed automatic transmission. That might not seem like a lot of power today, especially from a 5.0-liter V-8. However, an EFI Ford Mustang GT of the era was just barely producing 200 horsepower, making the SEC a serious muscle cruiser for its day.


There are certainly more powerful grand touring coupes out there, but few would make a statement like an SEC widebody. AMC-Exclusive went out of business in 1993, so these striking coupes are a rare sight. The long-lived W126 underpinnings, renowned for their reliable construction, make it easy to justify considering one of these Teutonic tuners for a collectible.


While ABC-exclusive used its own logo on some of its SECs, this coupe keeps its grille-mounted Mercedes Tri-Star. It also skipped the available hood scoop.


Broad Arrow
